title: What are the degree measures of the six angles?
description: Six angles named a to f are measured one by one with a protractor. The centre goes on the vertex, one arm goes on the zero line, and the number is read where the other arm crosses the scale. Each reading is then checked against a right angle.
teaching_notes: One idea: every angle is measured by the same three checks of the protractor, and each reading is checked against a right angle. Watch for students who read the scale that starts at the wrong end.

source: Figure it Out (after Angle Bisector), Q5
video_script.why: The child measures six angles with the protractor by the three checks of the solved example, and checks each reading against a right angle.
video_script.substitution: The six angles a, b, c, d, e and f of the book's question.
video_script.anchor: the six angles of the book, each with a small arc and the name a, b, c, d, e or f

final_answer.spoken: eighty, one hundred and twenty, sixty, one hundred and thirty, one hundred and thirty and sixty degrees

maths_rules: a right angle is 90 degrees; 80, 60 and 60 are less than 90, and 120, 130 and 130 are more than 90
the count starts at 0 on the arm that lies on the zero line
video_script.design: The six angles stay on the board. One protractor is placed on each in turn by the same steps, and the readings are held back until the answer line.

<bookmark mark='names'/>They are named eigh, bee, see, dee, ee and eff.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Before we measure, which angles look about the same size?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

<bookmark mark='centre'/>The centre of the protractor goes on the vertex.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>One arm goes along the zero line, and we read the scale that starts at that zero.

beats.on_screen: Given: six angles named a, b, c, d, e and f

marks.given: the six angle names are listed under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, six angles named eigh, bee, see, dee, ee and eff.

beats.on_screen: To find: the degree measure of each angle
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to measure each angle and write its degree measure.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: put the centre of the protractor on the vertex

marks.centre: the protractor slides until its centre point meets the vertex
marks.why: a tick appears beside the centre point

beats.moves_through: the protractor slides onto the vertex
narration: <bookmark mark='centre'/>Step one, put the centre of the protractor exactly on the vertex of the angle.
<bookmark mark='why'/>An angle is measured at its vertex, so the centre must sit there.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: turn the protractor until one arm lies along the 0 line

marks.turn: the protractor turns until one arm meets the zero line
marks.scale: the scale that starts at that zero is circled

beats.moves_through: the protractor turns about the vertex
narration: <bookmark mark='turn'/>Step two, turn the protractor until one arm lies along the zero line.
<bookmark mark='scale'/>We read the scale that starts at that zero.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: read the number on that scale where the other arm crosses it

marks.read: the other arm is followed out to the scale and the mark it crosses lights up

narration: <bookmark mark='read'/>Step three, follow the other arm out to the scale, and read the number where it crosses.
That number is the measure of the angle in degrees.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: repeat steps 1 to 3 for each of the six angles

marks.again: the protractor moves from angle a to b, c, d, e and f

beats.moves_through: the protractor moves from one angle to the next
narration: <bookmark mark='again'/>Step four, do the same three steps for each of the six angles, one after the other.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: check each reading with a right angle, 90°; narrower reads less than 90, wider reads more

marks.right: a right angle is drawn beside each angle
marks.check: a tick or a cross appears under each reading

narration: <bookmark mark='right'/>Step five, check each reading with a right angle, which is ninety degrees.
<bookmark mark='check'/>An angle narrower than a right angle must read less than ninety. A wider angle must read more.

marks.ans: the readings of a and b are boxed under their angles
marks.next: the readings of c and d are boxed under their angles
marks.last: the readings of e and f are boxed under their angles

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Angle eigh measures eighty degrees, and angle bee measures one hundred and twenty degrees.
<bookmark mark='next'/>Angle see measures sixty degrees, and angle dee measures one hundred and thirty degrees.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Angle ee measures one hundred and thirty degrees, and angle eff measures sixty degrees.
